prompt.context: Our client, Shermer Pharma, is a venture-backed start-up pharmaceutical company. Over the past 15 years, Shermer has been developing a molecule that has been approved by the FDA to cure Alzheimer's with 90% efficacy. The company has been purely a research firm to this point — it has no Sales or Marketing organization. FDA approval has been granted.
prompt.question: Shermer's owners have hired us to answer two questions: (1) How should we sell our product? (2) Is our product going to be profitable?

clarifying_info.a: A pill that cures Alzheimer's — an illness that currently has no treatment that cures or stops the progress of the disease.
Shermer will be the only firm with a cure for Alzheimer's for the next 5 years; we will not focus on competitive response.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the customers / targets for sales calls?
clarifying_info.a: Sales would be focused on Neurologists and Geriatric psychiatrists — not the consumer of the product.

clarifying_info.q: How large is the Alzheimer's market?
clarifying_info.a: 30 million people suffer worldwide. (Interviewer note: let the candidate try to size the market first, then provide the actual number of 5 million addressable users.)

clarifying_info.q: Does Shermer have any existing sales infrastructure?
clarifying_info.a: No. The company has been purely a research firm; there is no Sales or Marketing organization.

clarifying_info.q: What are the R&D costs that need to be recovered?
clarifying_info.a: $1.5 billion. The firm requires that R&D costs be recovered by Year 5 (straight-line amortization; ignore NPV).
We can ignore tax for this analysis.

clarifying_info.q: Are manufacturing and packaging costs included?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, manufacturing and packaging costs are included in the gross margin figure.

exhibits.title: Sales Force Options
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of two sales force options: Develop Own Sales Force vs. Contract Sales Force. Some cells are blank and must be calculated by the candidate.

rows.metric: Percent of visit focused on our product
Fully loaded annual cost of 1 sales rep

exhibits.title: Annual Net Income
exhibits.shows: A five-year P&L table with projected market penetration percentages filled in. All other rows (Total Users, Total Gross Margin, Amortized R&D Costs, Selling Costs, G&A Costs, Net Income) are blank and must be calculated by the candidate.

framework: Sales channel options: (1) develop own internal sales force, (2) use a contract sales organization, (3) sell Shermer to a larger firm with existing commercial infrastructure
Market sizing: estimate (or accept given figure of 5MM) addressable Alzheimer's patients to anchor revenue projections
Cost analysis — selling: use Exhibit 1 to calculate cost per sales call, total calls required, reps needed, and total annual selling cost for each option

Revenue and profitability (P&L): use Exhibit 2 to build a 5-year income statement — market penetration drives users, gross margin per user drives revenue, then subtract amortized R&D, selling costs, and G&A

Recommendation and risks: determine optimal sales channel based on cost and strategic fit; assess whether the product is profitable within the 5-year window; flag pricing and organizational considerations

questions.prompt: Walk through the sales force options. Which approach minimizes cost?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify three options: own sales force, contract sales, and selling the company. For Exhibit 1, they should fill in the missing cells. Own sales force: cost per sales call = $200k × 85 / 100 = $170; total calls required = 100k (given); total selling cost = $200k × 85 = $17MM. Contract sales: because reps spend only 50% of visit on the product, twice as many calls are needed — 200k; total reps = 170; total selling cost = $60 × 200k = $12MM. Contract sales is cheaper by $5MM/year. A strong candidate will also note that selling the company is an option even without hard data, and may qualitatively argue that the $5MM savings from contract sales is minimal relative to $3B revenues, so own sales force could be justified on effectiveness grounds.

math.setup: Own sales force: cost per call = annual rep cost × reps / total calls. Contract: double calls because 50% focus.
steps: Own cost per call = $200k × 85 reps / 100k calls = $170
math.answer: Contract sales costs $12MM/year vs. $17MM/year for own sales force; contract is cheaper by $5MM annually.

questions.prompt: Size the Alzheimer's market before receiving the given number.
questions.guidance: Candidate should attempt a market sizing: e.g., US population ~330M, ~15% over 65 (~50M), ~10% of those have Alzheimer's (~5M). The interviewer confirms 5MM addressable users after the attempt.

math.setup: Bottom-up or top-down sizing of Alzheimer's patients

questions.prompt: Build the 5-year P&L using Exhibit 2. Is the product profitable? Does Shermer recover R&D by Year 5?
questions.guidance: Candidate reads penetration percentages, calculates users (penetration × 5MM), gross margin (users × $1,000), then subtracts amortized R&D ($1.5B / 5 = $300MM/yr), selling costs ($12MM from contract), and G&A ($25MM). Year 1 is a loss; profitability is reached in Year 2; cumulative R&D is fully recovered by Year 5. Strong candidates note the $1,000 price point seems very low for a life-saving cure with no competition.

math.setup: Net Income = Gross Margin − Amortized R&D − Selling Costs − G&A. Using contract sales ($12MM/yr).
steps: Cumulative net Years 1–5: −$87MM+$163MM+$913MM+$1.663B+$2.663B = $5.315B — R&D fully recovered
math.answer: Product is profitable from Year 2 onward; cumulative profits well exceed the $1.5B R&D cost by Year 5.

brainstorming.prompt: What else should be considered before engaging this plan?

categories.name: Pricing strategy
ideas: $1,000/year appears under-priced for the only cure of a terminal illness
Explore value-based pricing given no competition for 5 years
Consider insurance reimbursement and payer dynamics

categories.name: Sales force effectiveness
ideas: Contract sales reps split attention across multiple products (50% focus)
Own sales force may yield higher conversion rates justifying $5MM premium
Incentive alignment differs between contract and internal reps

categories.name: Strategic alternatives
ideas: Selling Shermer to a larger pharma firm with existing commercial infrastructure
Partnering or co-promotion with an established firm

categories.name: Organizational build-out
ideas: Need to hire sales management and marketing leadership
Medical affairs and key opinion leader engagement
Market access and reimbursement team required

categories.name: Market and competitive risk
ideas: Competitor may enter before 5-year window expires

categories.name: Patient access
ideas: Alzheimer's patients often cannot self-administer; caregiver and institutional channel

recommendation: Shermer Pharma should use a contract sales force as its go-to-market channel; this minimizes annual selling costs at $12MM vs. $17MM for an internal force and avoids building commercial infrastructure the company has no experience with
Alternatively (and ideally), Shermer should consider selling the company to a larger pharmaceutical firm, which would maximize value given Shermer's core competency is research, not commercialization
The product will be profitable: it generates positive net income from Year 2 and recovers all $1.5B in R&D well before the end of Year 5
risks: Contract sales organization is typically less effective than an internal sales force — lower focus per call may slow market penetration
$1,000/year pricing may significantly undervalue the product; re-examine pricing before launch
Competitive entry before Year 5 would compress the profitability window
Building any commercial capability from scratch introduces execution risk
next_steps: Conduct pricing analysis to determine optimal price point (value-based approach given monopoly position)
Issue RFP to contract sales organizations and evaluate track record in neurology
Explore strategic acquirer conversations in parallel to retain optionality
Develop reimbursement and payer strategy with major insurers and Medicare/Medicaid
